as_told.title: John Alexander on the Hutchison experiments

plain: A man named John Hutchison was said to make objects float in the air, a claimed effect that came to carry his name, and a man named John B. Alexander was given the job of checking it. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and places Hutchison's work in California. A guest named Nick Cook says he later spoke to Alexander, who told him: "Unfortunately, when I set up all the equipment under laboratory conditions, none of it worked." Cook places the work in Vancouver rather than California. The story matters to the tellers because, if the effect were real, it would mean ordinary objects could be lifted against gravity.
